title: Map every 044 validation finding to a producer and test
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-cq3h
Spec ref:     specs/044-results-validation-errors.md#validation-finding-codes; specs/050-roundtrip-invariants.md#validation-on-write

Context:
The validation finding registry is only useful if every stable code has a runtime producer or an intentional documented deferral. This coverage audit exists to prevent agent-visible validation reports from drifting away from specs/044 and 050 as validators are implemented. It serves validate and write workflows by proving each finding code can be emitted, tested, or explicitly deferred without inventing ad-hoc codes.

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/validation/mod.rs (edit) — expose a test-only registry coverage table mapping every FindingCode to its producer function or deferral owner per specs/044.
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/validation/invariants.rs (edit) — add producer identifiers for invariant checks that emit 050/012/032/047/073 finding codes.
- crates/pptx-compose-core/tests/validation_registry_coverage.rs (new) — table-driven audit test proving all 044 registry codes are covered by a producer test or an explicit spec-backed deferral.

Change:
Add a non-runtime coverage map keyed by `FindingCode` from the 8agq registry. Each entry records `producer: Option<&'static str>`, `producer_test: Option<&'static str>`, and `deferral: Option<Deferral>` where a deferral must cite the owning bead/spec rule and explain why the code is not emitted yet. The initial audit must close the known gaps for `media_content_type_mismatch` (owned by media sniff validation per specs/032/044), `external_relationship_not_checked` (relationship preservation warning per specs/012/044/090), `invalid_bounds` (edit/DrawingML validation per specs/047/044), and `signature_invalidated_by_edit` (signed deck warning per specs/073/090). The test must fail if a FindingCode exists without exactly one of producer coverage or explicit deferral, and must assert no coverage entry names a code absent from specs/044. This task must not change validation severity semantics; it only verifies coverage against the canonical registry.

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-core --test validation_registry_coverage every_044_finding_has_producer_or_deferral` passes: all 15 specs/044 finding codes have either an executable producer test name or a documented deferral with spec reference, including media_content_type_mismatch, external_relationship_not_checked, invalid_bounds, and signature_invalidated_by_edit.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT implement missing validators here unless a tiny producer hook is required to make the coverage table compile; validator behavior belongs to ownx and dependent media/edit tasks. Do NOT add finding codes outside specs/044 or downgrade severities. Do NOT inspect or port legacy TypeScript validation behavior; this is a cleanroom audit of specs/044 and 050 coverage.

title: Enforce CLI runtime permission policy per 073
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-aitx
Spec ref:     specs/073-runtime-safety-and-permissions.md#filesystem-permission-model; specs/071-cli-agent-contract.md#global-rules

Context:
The CLI is an agent-facing filesystem surface, so path handling must be explicit and bounded before any PPTX read, media read, report write, diff write, or output write occurs. This exists to keep inspect/validate/apply/media operations inside the configured workspace and temp roots while preserving the no-prompt, machine-readable CLI contract. It serves parse, edit, validate, and write workflows by failing unsafe host interactions before package mutation.

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-cli/src/permissions.rs (new) — define CLI workspace/temp-root policy, path normalization, symlink handling, declared write-set checks, and temp cleanup helpers per specs/073.
- crates/pptx-compose-cli/src/cli.rs (edit) — add/parse `--keep-temp` as an explicit debug override alongside the existing `--workspace` and `--temp-dir` globals from specs/071.
- crates/pptx-compose-cli/src/main.rs (edit) — construct the permission context once and require command handlers to authorize input, output, media, report, diff, and temp paths before opening or writing.

Change:
Implement `struct PermissionContext { workspace: PathBuf, temp_dir: PathBuf, keep_temp: bool }` and `enum PathIntent { InputPptx, OutputPptx, MediaInput, ReportOutput, DiffOutput, TempFile }`. Add `PermissionContext::from_global_args(args: &GlobalArgs) -> Result<Self, CliError>`, `fn authorize_read(&self, path: &Path, intent: PathIntent) -> Result<PathBuf, CliError>`, `fn authorize_write(&self, path: &Path, intent: PathIntent) -> Result<PathBuf, CliError>`, and `fn cleanup_temp_on_failure(&self, temp_path: &Path) -> Result<(), CliError>`. Authorization must normalize paths, reject `~`/relative/platform aliases that escape the allowlist, resolve or reject symlinks before access, reject reads/writes outside `--workspace` or `--temp-dir`, and emit the 044 `permission_denied` or `unsafe_path` error codes that map to exit 3 in specs/071. The declared write set is limited to explicit output/report/diff paths, files under `--workspace`, temp files under `--temp-dir`, and stdout/stderr; failed writes remove partial temps unless `--keep-temp` is set. Byte-preservation is indirect here: this layer must not read/modify PPTX bytes itself, only authorize paths before the facade/core read-write path preserves clean parts.

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-cli permissions::rejects_escape_and_cleans_temp` passes: an outside-workspace read, a symlink escape, and an undeclared sibling write all return `permission_denied`/`unsafe_path`, and a failed temp output is removed unless `--keep-temp` is true.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT implement PPTX parsing, patch application, validation, or ZIP writes in the CLI permission layer. Do NOT expose unsafe validation bypass or raw XML mutation in the default CLI docs. Do NOT silently expand the declared write set by creating cache/extraction directories. Cleanroom: implement specs/073 and specs/071 behavior, do NOT port TypeScript path or fs behavior.

title: Implement public Rust facade API per 070
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-aitx
Spec ref:     specs/070-public-api-and-cli.md#rust-api; specs/070-public-api-and-cli.md#write-and-open-modes

Context:
Spec 070 defines the public Rust facade as the stable entrypoint that CLI and MCP surfaces should depend on instead of reaching into OPC/XML internals. This task gives agents and downstream callers one safe workflow-shaped API for parse, agent-view, edit, validate, and write. It also centralizes the default preservation and validation behavior required by specs/020, 044, 050, and 070.

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose/src/lib.rs (edit) — define `PresentationDocument` and the required public facade methods from specs/070 while keeping internal parser types out of the primary API.
- crates/pptx-compose/src/options.rs (new) — define `OpenOptions`, `AgentViewOptions`, `ApplyPatchOptions`, `WriteMode`, and `WriteOptions` with the spec-070 defaults.
- crates/pptx-compose/tests/facade_api.rs (new) — compile/API tests for the required method surface and default option values.

Change:
Implement the facade in the `pptx-compose` crate with these public signatures, adjusted only for concrete error/report/view types already defined by dependent crates: `PresentationDocument::open_path(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Self, Error>`, `open_path_with_options(path: impl AsRef<Path>, options: OpenOptions) -> Result<Self, Error>`, `from_bytes(bytes: impl AsRef<[u8]>) -> Result<Self, Error>`, `open_reader<R: Read>(reader: R) -> Result<Self, Error>`, `to_agent_json(&self) -> Result<serde_json::Value, Error>`, `to_agent_json_with_options(&self, options: AgentViewOptions) -> Result<serde_json::Value, Error>`, `to_legacy_json(&self) -> Result<serde_json::Value, Error>`, `apply_patch(&mut self, patch: Patch, media: MediaInputs) -> Result<PatchReport, Error>`, `apply_patch_with_options(&mut self, patch: Patch, media: MediaInputs, options: ApplyPatchOptions) -> Result<PatchReport, Error>`, `validate(&self) -> Result<ValidationReport, Error>`, `write_path(&self, path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<(), Error>`, `write_path_with_options(&self, path: impl AsRef<Path>, options: WriteOptions) -> Result<(), Error>`, `write_vec(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error>`, and `write_vec_with_options(&self, options: WriteOptions) -> Result<Vec<u8>, Error>`. `WriteMode` must be `Preserve` by default, `WriteOptions` defaults must be `overwrite=false`, `validate=true`, and `atomic=true`, and deterministic mode must never re-serialize clean part payloads; clean payload byte preservation remains owned by the core XML/ZIP tasks this facade calls. `apply_patch*` and `validate` must return the structured report/error types from specs/044 rather than `Result<()>`, and CLI/MCP should be able to use this facade without importing `pptx_compose_core::opc`, `xml`, or `zip` modules directly.

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose --test facade_api exposes_required_070_api_and_defaults` passes: the test type-checks every required facade method, asserts `WriteOptions::default()` is `{ mode: Preserve, overwrite: false, validate: true, atomic: true }`, and verifies the facade crate can be used without naming internal OPC/XML/ZIP parser types.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT implement new OPC parsing, ZIP writing, XML serialization, edit operations, validation rules, CLI commands, or MCP tools in the facade; delegate to the owning crates and return their structured reports/errors. Do NOT expose raw XML mutation as the default API or allow validation bypass except through an explicit unsafe/debug option. Cleanroom: implement the API contract from specs/070 and boundary rules from specs/060; do NOT port TypeScript implementation details or line-by-line behavior.

title: Enforce no-inline-binary rule (media-by-reference)
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-ljyc
Spec ref:     specs/040-agent-json-format.md#binary-handling (+ specs/042#image-element-view)

Context:
Agent JSON must never blow the context window or leak raw bytes: binary media is referenced by media part + checksum + content-type, not inlined as base64. This task enforces the no-inline-binary invariant in the agent-view image projection and provides the explicit opt-in escape hatch. Serves the agent-view read path and the media-by-reference contract.

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-json/src/agent_view/mod.rs (edit) — ImageView carries relationship_id, media_part, content_type, byte_length, checksum, intrinsic_size_px, shared_media_ref_count and NO bytes/data field by default. Implements specs/042 image-element-view.
- crates/pptx-compose-json/src/binary_encoding.rs (new) — InlineBinaryPolicy enum; only the opt-in path emits any base64 payload. Implements specs/040 binary-handling.

Change:
Make ImageView a pure media-reference struct per specs/042: relationship_id, media_part, content_type, byte_length: u64, checksum: "sha256:…", intrinsic_size_px: Option<{width,height}>, shared_media_ref_count: u32 — no byte/data field. Introduce enum InlineBinaryPolicy { ByReference, InlineBase64 } with Default = ByReference; the standard view builders always use ByReference and emit zero base64. Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-json agent_view::binary::no_inline_by_default` passes: serializing an AgentView containing an image yields JSON with media_part + checksum + byte_length and zero base64 payloads (assert no "$binary"/"data" key and no string field over a small char threshold); switching to InlineBase64 is the only way to obtain a data payload.

Risks / out of scope:
Agent-view image references only — the legacy $binary envelope is h5xt; the media-staging crate is separate. Do NOT inline bytes in any standard view mode. Cleanroom: per specs/040 binary-handling, not TS Buffer/Uint8Array behavior.

title: Atomic writes + no implicit overwrite + --deterministic

title: Magic-byte content-type verification PNG/JPEG/GIF
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-vqpb
Spec ref:     specs/032-media-images.md#add-image-operation (also specs/043-media-staging-and-refs.md#media-ref-rules; specs/044-results-validation-errors.md)

Context:
A staged media input declares a content type, but an agent can declare the wrong one
or supply an unsupported format. Per specs/032 and /043 the declared content type
must be verified against the file's magic bytes where feasible before the image is
added to a slide. Serves the edit/apply step by failing bad media at staging rather
than corrupting the deck (P2).

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-edit/src/media_inputs/sniff.rs (new) — magic-byte sniffer for
  the V1 raster formats, per specs/032 supported-input list.
- crates/pptx-compose-edit/src/media_inputs/mod.rs (edit) — call the sniffer from
  `MediaInputs::resolve` (zajk) so every resolved binding is verified.

Change:
- `fn sniff_content_type(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<&'static str>` recognizing PNG
  (`89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A` -> image/png), JPEG (`FF D8 FF` -> image/jpeg), and
  GIF (`47 49 46 38` [GIF8] -> image/gif); returns None for anything else.
- `fn verify_declared(declared: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Error>`: if the
  sniffed type is None (or not in the V1 supported set PNG/JPEG/GIF), return
  `Error::unsupported_media_type` (exit 23 per specs/071); if a type is sniffed but
  disagrees with `declared`, return an error carrying the canonical finding code
  `media_content_type_mismatch` (specs/044, codes 012/032). Wire this into resolve()
  so it runs before any mutation.

  structure — only the leading signature per specs/032 "where feasible".

`cargo test -p pptx-compose-edit media_inputs::sniff::detects_and_rejects` passes:
PNG/JPEG/GIF signature bytes sniff to the correct content type; declaring image/png

errors with `unsupported_media_type`.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT add SVG/TIFF/EMF/WMF/HEIC support (specs/032: preserve-only in V1) — they
sniff to unsupported. Do NOT re-encode or transcode bytes. Do NOT touch the read
side (core pptx/media exposing existing pictures). Cleanroom: implement the specs/032
magic-byte rule, not any TS sniffing helper.

title: rId allocation policy (rId{max+1}, collision-safe, deterministic)
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-rbj9
Spec ref:     specs/012-content-types-and-relationships.md#relationship-id-allocation

Context:
When an edit adds a relationship (add_image, add_text_box, replace_image, 041; and
DrawingML construction, 047) it needs a fresh, collision-free, deterministic rId so
tests can assert exact values and re-runs are reproducible. This task implements the
allocation policy on the RelationshipSet from 21uo. opc layer only; the edit
operations call it.

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/opc/relationships.rs (edit) — add the allocator
  method to RelationshipSet from 21uo, implementing spec 012 "Relationship ID
  Allocation".

Change:
- `RelationshipSet::allocate_id(&self) -> String`:
  1. Scan existing ids; parse those matching `^rId(\d+)$` into their integer suffix.
  2. `m` = max parsed suffix, or 0 if none match; candidate is `rId{m+1}`.
  3. If the candidate collides with ANY existing id (including non-conforming ids
     that are literally `rId{m+1}`), increment the numeric suffix until free.
  4. Pure function of current state: same set + same call sequence => same ids.
- Allocation does not mutate; the caller adds the Relationship with the returned id.
  Allocation is per RelationshipSet (per relationship part), never global.

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-core opc::relationships::allocate_id` passes:
{rId1, rId2, rId5} -> "rId6"; {} -> "rId1"; a set whose ids are {rId1, "rId2x",
rId2 literal as non-conforming} still returns the first free `rId{n}` and never
duplicates an existing id.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT insert the relationship or touch [Content_Types].xml here — only compute the
id. Do NOT make allocation depend on global package state. Cleanroom: follow the
spec 012 algorithm exactly, not any TS id-generation behavior.

description:

Context:
Full-deck export is not the agent read path for large decks. Agents must page through slides/elements/findings and see explicit truncation markers instead of silent omission. description:

Context:
Agent IDs are the stable string identifiers an agent uses to target slides, elements,

stable structural position, never from reassignable OOXML ids. The element-id-from-path
helper (agent_element_id) and spTree indexing already exist in pptx::ids (epic prp4);
this task adds slide-id and paragraph/run-id derivation and wires the full chain. Serves
the agent-view and edit-targeting workflows.

- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/pptx/ids.rs (edit) - add slide-id + paragraph/run-id
  derivation alongside the existing index_sp_tree / agent_element_id.

- fn slide_agent_id(presentation_order_index: usize) -> String returning

agent_element_id (already in pptx::ids from prp4). Cleanroom: implement the 046 rule.

title: Text reading: paragraphs/runs positional identity + normalized/plain
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-prp4
Spec ref:     specs/031-slides-shapes-and-text.md#text-reading; specs/042-agent-protocol-schemas.md#text-element-view; specs/046-provenance-and-hashing.md#text_hash

Context:
Projects a shape's a:txBody into the structured text view (paragraphs/runs with
positional ids and plain/normalized projections) agents read and target. The normalized
projection is the exact preimage the provenance epic later hashes into text_hash, so it
must match 046 byte-for-byte. Serves parse -> agent-view and text-edit targeting.

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/pptx/text.rs (new) - TextBody, Paragraph, Run,
  RunStyleSummary, plain/normalized projection.

Change:
- struct Run { index: u32 /* a:r ordinal */, text: String, style_summary: RunStyleSummary }.
- struct Paragraph { index: u32 /* a:p ordinal */, runs: Vec<Run> }.
- struct TextBody { paragraphs: Vec<Paragraph>, plain: String, normalized: String }.
- fn read_text_body(txbody: &XmlElement) -> TextBody: collect a:p in document order

title: Per-surface stale-patch rule (MCP rejects on mismatch)
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-uild
Spec ref:     specs/072-mcp-server-contract.md#sessions-and-revisions, specs/041-agent-edit-operations.md

Context:
Enforces optimistic-concurrency safety on the MCP surface: a patch whose base_revision
does not match the session's current revision is rejected with stale_patch and never
silently rebased. Serves the edit/apply workflow by guaranteeing an agent cannot apply
against a stale view.

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs (edit) -- pptx_apply_patch / pptx_validate_patch revision guard

Change:
- In pptx_apply_patch and pptx_validate_patch, before delegating to the edit engine, compare patch.base_revision (or expected_revision) to the session's current revision under the per-session lock.
- On mismatch, return the 044 canonical stale_patch error envelope (via 7m0k map_error); do NOT rebase, retry, or mutate session state. Include current_revision in error details so the agent can re-fetch.
- On match, proceed; only a successful non-dry-run apply increments revision (owned by s7uj). Serialize concurrent applies so two in-flight patches at the same base revision cannot both succeed.

Acceptance:
cargo test -p pptx-compose-mcp tools::apply_rejects_stale_revision passes: opening (rev 1), applying a patch with base_revision 1 succeeds and moves to rev 2; a second patch still carrying base_revision 1 returns a stale_patch envelope and leaves revision at 2.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT implement auto-rebase or force-apply. Do NOT duplicate revision-increment logic (own it in s7uj). Operation application itself lives in pptx-compose-edit -- this task only adds the guard + rejection at the MCP boundary. Cleanroom: rule per spec 072, not TS behavior.

Parent epic:  pptx-compose-erdf

Context:

title: Compute text_hash over NFC/whitespace-normalized text projection
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-gvtc
Spec ref:     specs/046-provenance-and-hashing.md#text_hash, specs/042-agent-protocol-schemas.md#text-element-view

Context:
text_hash is the digest of an element's normalized text projection. It backs the
`normalized` field exposed in the agent text view (042) and is one of the two selector
guards (with fingerprint) that detect element substitution before an edit. The same
normalization must define both the hashed bytes and the 042 field so they never diverge.
Serves the agent-view and selector-guard workflows.

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/provenance/text_hash.rs (new) - normalized projection +
  its digest.

Change:
- fn normalize_text(runs: &[&str], has_br: &[bool]) -> String (or an equivalent run-model
  input): concatenate run text in document order, then apply 046 normalization - Unicode
  NFC; collapse each run of XML whitespace (U+0020, U+0009, U+000A, U+000D) to a single
  U+0020; trim leading/trailing whitespace of the whole projection. A soft line break
  (`a:br`) projects as a single U+000A that is PRESERVED (not collapsed), so multi-line
  text stays distinguishable.
- fn text_hash(normalized: &str) -> String = provenance::cpj::digest_prefixed over the
  UTF-8 bytes of the normalized projection.
- The normalize_text output is exactly the 042 `normalized` field; `plain` (042) is the
  unnormalized concatenation and is never hashed here.

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-core provenance::text_hash::normalization` passes: runs
["  Hello\t", "\n world "] normalize to "Hello world"; a two-paragraph element joined by
an a:br normalizes to "line1\nline2" (the \n preserved); and text_hash of the result
equals the precomputed `sha256:` constant. NFC: a decomposed e+combining-acute hashes
equal to the precomposed e-acute.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT collapse the a:br newline; do NOT hash `plain`; do NOT apply locale-dependent
casing/folding (046: reproducible from bytes alone). Run/paragraph indexing belongs to
ids (gqyp), not here. Cleanroom: implement the 046/042 normalization rule.

description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-gvtc
Spec ref:     specs/046-provenance-and-hashing.md#fingerprint

Context:

(041/042): when a stale agent element ID points at a location, a fingerprint mismatch
means the element there is no longer the one the agent saw, so the engine returns
selector_guard_failed (044) instead of a best-effort edit. Serves the selector-guard /
safe-edit workflow.

- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/provenance/fingerprint.rs (new) - fingerprint CPJ + digest.

- struct FingerprintInput { kind: ElementKind, part: PartName, sp_tree_path: Vec<u32>,

  "group"|...>, "part": <canonical PartName>, "schema": "pptx-compose.fingerprint.v1",

title: Implement Canonical Preimage JSON (CPJ) encoder and SHA-256 digest primitive
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-gvtc
Spec ref:     specs/046-provenance-and-hashing.md#hash-primitive, specs/046-provenance-and-hashing.md#canonical-preimage-encoding

Context:
Several provenance values (document_id, fingerprint, view_id) hash a structured
preimage rather than raw bytes. This task provides the single Canonical Preimage
JSON (CPJ) encoder and the SHA-256 digest primitive that every other 046 value is
built on, so digests are stable across implementations and across a no-edit round
trip. Serves the validate / round-trip / guard workflows (all identity comparisons).

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/provenance/cpj.rs (new) - CPJ encoder + digest helper.
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/provenance/mod.rs (new) - module exports (re-exports
  cpj/checksum/document_id/text_hash/fingerprint/view_id/revision as siblings land).

Change:
- enum Cpj { Null, Int(i64), Str(String), Array(Vec<Cpj>), Object(BTreeMap<String,Cpj>) }
  - a value model that excludes floats by construction (046: "No floating-point values
  appear in any preimage").
- fn encode(value: &Cpj) -> Vec<u8>: emit UTF-8 with object keys sorted by Unicode code
  point ascending (BTreeMap already enforces this), no insignificant whitespace, minimal
  escaping (only `"`, `\`, and U+0000-U+001F control chars; non-ASCII emitted raw, not
  \u-escaped), integers base-10 with no leading zeros / no `+`, arrays in given order.
- fn sha256_hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String using the `sha2` crate, returning the 64-char
  lowercase hex digest.
- fn digest_prefixed(bytes: &[u8]) -> String returning `sha256:` + sha256_hex(bytes).
- fn digest_cpj(value: &Cpj) -> String = digest_prefixed(&encode(value)).
  This is the canonical preimage path used by document_id/fingerprint/view_id.

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-core provenance::cpj::canonical_encoding` passes: a fixed
nested Cpj object with out-of-order keys and a non-ASCII string encodes to the exact
expected canonical byte string (keys sorted, no whitespace, raw UTF-8), and
digest_cpj of the empty object equals the SHA-256 of `{}` with the `sha256:` prefix.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT use serde_json::Value directly as the public preimage type (its f64 number arm
would admit floats and its default key order is insertion order) - the BTreeMap-backed
Cpj enum is what guarantees 046's no-float / sorted-key invariants. Do NOT \u-escape
non-ASCII. No other provenance value is computed here (siblings consume this). Cleanroom:
implement the 046 encoding rules, do NOT port any TS serializer.

title: Deterministic media part naming + opt-in dedup
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-vqpb
Spec ref:     specs/043-media-staging-and-refs.md#deterministic-media-part-naming (also specs/032-media-images.md#deduplication)

Context:
When an add/replace-image op commits a staged media input it must choose a new media
part name that is deterministic and collision-safe so repeated runs over the same
input produce byte-identical packages, and it may optionally reuse an existing part
when checksums match. Per specs/043 the policy is `ppt/media/image{next}.{ext}` with
collision checks; per specs/032 dedup must never silently merge parts by default.
Serves the edit/apply step's determinism and round-trip stability (P2).

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/pptx/media.rs (new) — deterministic media-part
  naming and opt-in checksum dedup over the PartStore, per specs/043 + /032.

Change:
- `fn next_media_part_name(parts: &PartStore, ext: &str) -> PartName`: scan existing
  `ppt/media/image{N}.{ext}` parts (and names already allocated this request) and
  return `ppt/media/image{max_seen+1}.{ext}`, lowercasing the extension and choosing
  it from the resolved content type (image/png->png, image/jpeg->jpeg, image/gif->gif)
  per specs/032 supported set. Allocation is deterministic given the same starting
  PartStore and insertion order; it must be collision-safe against existing parts
  AND parts staged earlier in the same apply.
- `fn dedup_lookup(parts: &PartStore, sha256: &str, opt_in: bool) -> Option<PartName>`:
  only when `opt_in` is true, return an existing media part whose content matches the
  digest (reuse instead of adding); when false, always return None so a new part is
  named — never silently merge (specs/032).
- Consumes the digest computed by y0dm; does not recompute hashing policy.

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-core pptx::media::names_deterministically_and_dedups`
passes: with `image1.png`/`image2.png` present, naming a new png yields
`ppt/media/image3.png`; the result is identical across repeated calls on an equal
store; with dedup off a byte-identical asset still gets a fresh name; with dedup on it
resolves to the existing matching part.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT default dedup on, and do NOT merge visually-identical-but-byte-different media
(specs/032). Do NOT write content-type or relationship entries here (rbj9 xujw/fhm4
and the add-image op own those) — this only picks the name and optional reuse target.
Cleanroom: implement the specs/043 naming policy, not any TS naming scheme.

title: Content-type resolution algorithm (Override -> Default case-insensitive ext -> untyped)
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-rbj9
Spec ref:     specs/012-content-types-and-relationships.md#content-type-resolution-algorithm

Context:
Every ordinary part must resolve to exactly one content type, and the order
(Override exact -> Default by extension -> untyped) is normative. This is the
single function the validation layer (r5bi / missing_content_type) and the writer
call to answer "what is this part's content type?". Builds directly on the parsed
ContentTypes table (tv4w). opc layer only.

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-core/src/opc/content_types.rs (edit) — add the resolution
  method to the ContentTypes model from tv4w, implementing spec 012's 3-step order.

Change:
- `ContentTypes::resolve(&self, part: &PartName) -> Option<&str>`:
  1. Override exact match: if `overrides` contains `part` (canonical name, leading
     slash, case-SENSITIVE per 010), return that MIME.
  2. Default by extension: take the substring after the final `.` of the part name;
     if empty/absent, no extension match. Lowercase it and look up `defaults`
     (keys stored lowercased by tv4w) so PNG/png/Png all hit Default `png`.
  3. Untyped: return None. Resolution never errors; the missing-content-type
     condition becomes a validation finding (r5bi), not a parse error.
- Override beats Default whenever both apply (step 1 returns before step 2). The
  extension comparison is the ONLY case-insensitive comparison; segment matching
  in step 1 stays case-sensitive.

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-core opc::content_types::resolution_order` passes,
asserting: an Override on /ppt/slides/slide1.xml wins over any Default; a part
/ppt/media/image1.PNG resolves via Default `png`; a part with an unknown extension
resolves to None.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT emit the missing_content_type finding here (that is r5bi) — just return
None. Do NOT add any default/override entries. Do NOT lowercase the part name
itself, only the extension used for the Default lookup. Cleanroom: follow spec
012, not legacy TS resolution quirks.

title: Checksum handling + media_checksum_mismatch before mutation
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-vqpb
Spec ref:     specs/043-media-staging-and-refs.md#media-ref-rules (also specs/044-results-validation-errors.md; specs/071-cli-agent-contract.md#exit-codes)

Context:
When a manifest or MCP media handle declares a `sha256`, the bytes actually bound to
that `media_ref` must match it, so an agent cannot stage one asset and apply a
different one. Per specs/043 a checksum mismatch is a HARD error and per specs/043 it
must be detected before any package mutation. Serves the edit/apply step's integrity
(P2).

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-edit/src/media_inputs/mod.rs (edit) — compute and compare the
  digest inside `MediaInputs::resolve` (zajk), using the verified sha2 crate.

Change:
- In `resolve`, when a binding carries `declared_sha256`, compute
  `sha256:<hex>` over the resolved bytes (sha2 crate, lowercase hex, `sha256:` prefix
  to match the manifest/handle format in specs/043) and compare constant-form to the
  declared value. On mismatch return `Error::media_checksum_mismatch` (exit 23 per
  specs/071) naming the media_ref plus the expected and actual digests — emitted
  BEFORE any PartStore mutation. When `declared_sha256` is absent, skip the check
  (checksum is optional per specs/043) but still return the computed digest on the
  `ResolvedMedia` so downstream naming/dedup (w3sl) can reuse it.
- Reuse the same digest helper the provenance epic standardized; do not invent a
  second hashing format.

Acceptance:
`cargo test -p pptx-compose-edit media_inputs::checksum::mismatch_fails_before_mutation`
passes: bytes whose digest matches the declared `sha256:` resolve and expose the
computed digest; bytes whose digest differs from a declared value return
`Error::media_checksum_mismatch`; a binding with no declared sha256 resolves and
still reports a computed digest.

Risks / out of scope:
Do NOT mutate the package or name parts here (w3sl / add-image own that) — the point
is that the failure happens first. Do NOT use a non-sha256 digest or omit the
`sha256:` prefix. Cleanroom: implement the specs/043 checksum rule, not any TS hash
helper.

title: media_ref binding across Rust/CLI/MCP (manifest + inline)
description:
Parent epic:  pptx-compose-vqpb
Spec ref:     specs/043-media-staging-and-refs.md#media-ref-rules (also #rust-api-media-inputs)

Context:
Patch operations reference media by `media_ref` keys, never by inlined bytes in the
operation. This task builds the foundational `MediaInputs` resolver that every other
media task consumes: it binds each `media_ref` to a concrete byte source (path,
in-memory bytes, or reader) for one apply/dry-run request or one MCP session, and
resolves it BEFORE the package is mutated. Serves the edit/apply step; correctness
of edits depends on it, but it is a staging primitive (P2).

Target crate / files:
- crates/pptx-compose-edit/src/media_inputs/mod.rs (new) — the `MediaInputs` type
  and resolution logic, per specs/043 media-ref rules.
- crates/pptx-compose-edit/src/media_inputs/manifest.rs (new) — parse the
  `pptx-compose.media_manifest.v1` manifest and inline-base64 form into bindings.

Change:
- `enum MediaSource { Path(PathBuf), Bytes(Vec<u8>), InlineBase64(String) }` and
  `struct MediaBinding { content_type: String, declared_sha256: Option<String>,
  declared_byte_length: Option<u64>, source: MediaSource }`.

  `fn from_manifest(manifest: &MediaManifest, media_root: &Path) -> Result<Self,Error>`
  and `fn resolve(&self, media_ref: &str) -> Result<ResolvedMedia, Error>` returning
  the bound bytes + content type. Per specs/043: a `media_ref` with no binding fails
  with `Error::missing_media_ref` (exit 23 per specs/071) BEFORE any mutation; a

passes: a `MediaInputs` built from a 2-key manifest resolves both keys to their

a manifest with a duplicate key returns `Error::invalid_input`.

Do NOT mutate the package, allocate part names, or write media parts here (w3sl /
the add-image op own that). Do NOT resolve paths that escape `--media-root` (that
guard is part of manifest path handling — reject as `unsafe_path`). Cleanroom:
implement the specs/043 ref model, not any TS media helper.
